look_here_first: MUCRONATE SPRANGLETOP: native-at-state-scale slender warm-season ANNUAL with many almost straight, very fine ascending branches arranged along a central flowering axis. Close inspection of the 2–4-flowered tiny spikelet reveals an upper glume with minute MUCRONATE projection, which is NOT visible in the current overall photo. Formerly Leptochloa mucronata; don't duplicate.

crew_field_check: Unlike perennial Disakisperma dubium (which can have similar slender flowering branches) this is an annual, with a delicate brushlike set of closely spaced thin branches; Disakisperma has 4–13-flowered spikelets and may produce hidden flowers in lower sheaths. Distinguish against other Dinebra/Leptochloa using true glume and lemma anatomy.
Confirm true collar, ripe spikelets and habit from the same source-identified individual.
